title: Precision Bookmarking and Mini-Batch Kernel Heuristics for INT8/FP8 Fanout
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Background: Mixed-precision execution (INT8/FP8) delivers large cost and throughput wins but we pay repeated dequant/requant costs at attention/KV boundaries. Variable token fanout during decoding (long-horizon vs short-horizon requests, chat vs system prompts) frustrates static kernel selection heuristics and forces either conservative FP32 fallbacks or expensive cross-precision transitions.

Proposal summary: Implement a lightweight "precision bookmarking" metadata slot on KV cache entries plus a mini-batch kernel heuristic in the runtime kernel selector. The design bookmarks segments of the KV cache with their native precision and propagation horizon so the selector can avoid unnecessary dequant/requant for slices of the batch. The kernel heuristic will consider token fanout distribution, remaining decode horizon, and a latency budget to pick a mixed-precision kernel plan per minibatch (or sub-minibatch) rather than per-request.

Goals: reduce end-to-end decode latency (p95/p99) and per-token GPU cost in workloads with heterogeneous decode lengths, while keeping quality regressions under our threshold and preserving deterministic outputs for pinned model versions.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime supports a KV metadata bookmark flag and stores precision + horizon window per KV slab
Kernel selector implements mini-batch scoring and can choose different kernels for sub-slices of a minibatch
Unit + integration tests covering precision bookmark lifecycles and fallbacks
Benchmarks show >=5% p95 latency improvement on mixed-horizon chat workload and >=10% reduction in amortized dequant GPU cycles in internal perf suite
No quality regression >0.5% on our eval prompts (same seed, model pinned) when switching kernels; documented deviations accepted by ML owner
Feature gated behind runtime feature flag and rollout via canary A/B with telemetry dashboards
